name: The Cypress Cove Special Purpose District
source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 818 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 818.

PD 818.

The Cypress Cove Special Purpose District.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 818 was established by Ordinance No. 27921, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 23, 2010. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 818 is established on property generally located east of Bobtown Road and north of Barnes Bridge Road between the City of Garland to the north and west and the Town of Sunnyvale to the south. The size of PD 818 is approximately 267.019 acres. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Creation Of Subdistricts
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.103. CREATION OF SUBDISTRICTS.

This district is divided into three subdistricts: Subdistrict 1, Subdistrict 2, and Subdistrict 3. The boundaries of each subdistrict are illustrated on the conceptual plan (Exhibit 818A). Verbal descriptions of the subdistrict boundaries are provided in Exhibit 818B. If there is a conflict between the conceptual plan and the verbal descriptions in Exhibit 818B, Exhibit 818B controls. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) 40-FOOT WIDE LOTS means lots that are at least 40 feet in width but less than 50 feet in width measured from the front building line.

(2) 50-FOOT WIDE LOTS means lots that are at least 50 feet in width but less than 60 feet in width measured from the front building line.

(3) 60-FOOT WIDE LOTS means lots that are at least 60 feet in width measured from the front building line.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.105. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 818A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 818B: subdistrict boundaries. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 818A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Subdistricts 1 and 2. The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in these subdistricts only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-7.5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in these subdistricts; etc.

(b) Subdistrict 3. The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the MF-3(A) Multifamily District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-3(A) Multifamily District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MF-3(A) Multifamily District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-3(A) Multifamily District is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.109. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are permitted by SUP only:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Amateur communication tower. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.110. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Maximum number of dwelling units is 1,026.

(b) Subdistrict 1.

(1) In general.

(A) Density. The maximum density is 721 lots.

(B) Distribution of lot types.

(1) Minimum number of 60-foot-wide lots is 227.

(2) Maximum number of 50-foot-wide lots is 494.

(3) Maximum number of 40-foot-wide lots is 206.

(2) 60-foot wide lots.

(A) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 20 feet. Covered, unenclosed porches may extend eight feet into the required front yard.

(B) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard is five feet. Minimum rear yard is 10 feet.

(C) Floor area. Minimum floor area for a single-family unit is 1,800 square feet of air-conditioned space.

(D) Height. Maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(E) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(F) Lot size. Minimum lot width is 60 feet. Minimum lot depth is 115 feet.

(G) Garage door setback. Minimum garage door setback is 10 feet from an alley and 18 feet from a street right-of-way. Garage doors for a residential use located less than 20 feet from a street or alley must be equipped with an automatic garage door opener. The automatic garage door opener must be maintained in working order at all times. For purposes of this section, a garage means a parking space or spaces located in an enclosed structure.

(2) 50-foot wide lots.

(A) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 20 feet. Covered, unenclosed porches may extend eight feet into the required front yard.

(B) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard is five feet. Minimum rear yard is 10 feet.

(C) Floor area. Minimum floor area for a single-family unit is 1,500 square feet of air-conditioned space.

(D) Height. Maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(E) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(F) Lot size. Minimum lot width is 50 feet. Minimum lot depth is 110 feet.

(G) Garage door setback. Minimum garage door setback is 10 feet from an alley and 18 feet from a street right-of-way. Garage doors for a residential use located less than 20 feet from a street or alley must be equipped with an automatic garage door opener. The automatic garage door opener must be maintained in working order at all times. For purposes of this section, a garage means a parking space or spaces located in an enclosed structure.

(3) 40-foot wide lots.

(A) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 15 feet. Covered, unenclosed porches may extend eight feet into the required front yard.

(B) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard is five feet. Minimum rear yard is 10 feet.

(C) Floor area. Minimum floor area for a single-family unit is 1,500 square feet of air-conditioned space.

(D) Height. Maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(E) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 65 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(F) Lot size. Minimum lot width is 40 feet. Minimum lot depth is 110 feet.

(G) Garage door setback. Minimum garage door setback is 10 feet from an alley. Garage doors for a residential uses located less than 20 feet from a street or alley must be equipped with an automatic garage door opener. The automatic garage door opener must be maintained in working order at all times. For purposes of this section, a garage means a parking space or spaces located in an enclosed structure.

(c) Subdistrict 2.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-1/2ac(A) Single Family District apply.

(2) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 30 feet.

(d) Subdistrict 3.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, the yard, lot, and space regulations for an MF-3(A) Multifamily District apply.

(2) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, see Article VI.

(b) To the greatest extent possible, development must be fitted to the topography and soils to minimize cut and fill sections.

(c) Grading is limited to areas where a final plat has been filed in the county records. Grading must be planned to have the least disturbance on the area’s natural topography, watercourses, vegetation, and wildlife.

(d) Indigenous vegetation must be retained and protected except in immediate areas of development so that a minimal amount of vegetation is removed or replaced.

(e) Development must be accomplished in a manner which assures that as small an area as possible is exposed to erosion at any one time. When land is exposed during development, the exposure must be kept to the shortest practical period of time not to exceed 12 months. In extraordinary cases, an extension of the 12 month time period may be granted in writing by the director if the director finds that the delay is caused by circumstances beyond the control of the applicant. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Single family uses. A lot containing a single family use must have at least three trees with a caliper equal to or exceeding three inches. At least two trees must be located in the front yard.

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(d) Landscaping in the public right-of-way.

(1) Private license granted.

(A) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners or tenants (with the written consent of the owner) of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing monument features, entrance signage, landscaping, and irrigation in the public right-of-way. “Parkway” means the portion of a street right-of-way between the street curb and the lot line. An owner or tenant is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a parkway landscape permit. This private license will not terminate at the end of any specific period, however, the city council reserves the right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city council of

the need for termination is final and binding. The city shall become entitled to possession of the licensed area without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession when, in its judgment, the purpose or use of the license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of the license is likely to become a nuisance or a threat to public safety. Upon termination of the license by the city council, each owner or tenant shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(B) An owner or tenant is not required to comply with any landscaping requirement to the extent that compliance is made impossible due to the city council's revocation of the private license granted by this subsection.

(C) Upon the installation of landscaping and related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the owner or tenant shall procure, pay for, and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the private license granted under this subsection, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence, and $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy must be on an occurrence basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance must be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, Dallas, Texas 75201, and the policy must provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent that they are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(D) Each owner or tenant is responsible for maintaining the landscaping in a healthy, growing condition, for keeping related amenities in good repair and condition, and for keeping the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city. The city is absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping, related amenities, or the premises. The granting of a license for landscaping and related amenities under this subsection does not release the owner or tenant from liability for the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, and related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(2) Parkway landscape permit.

(A) It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain a parkway landscape permit before locating trees, landscaping, or related amenities in the parkway. An application for a parkway landscape permit must be made to the building official. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the building official and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the planting or other amenities proposed.

(B) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the building official shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If,

after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the building official determines that the construction, planting, or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the building official shall issue a parkway landscape permit to the property owner; otherwise, the building official shall deny the permit.

(C) A property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this article if compliance is made impossible due to the building official's denial of a parkway landscape permit.

(D) A parkway landscape permit issued by the building official is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if at any time the building official determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right-of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this article if compliance is made impossible due to the building official's revocation of a parkway landscape permit.

(E) The issuance of a parkway landscape permit under this subsection does not excuse the property owner, his agents, or employees from liability for the installation or maintenance of trees or other amenities in the public right-of-way. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Tree Mitigation And Protection
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.114. TREE MITIGATION AND PROTECTION.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, tree mitigation must be provided in accordance with Articles V and X.

(2) Except as provided in Paragraph (3), this section applies to all property within this district.

(3) This section does not apply to lots smaller than two acres that have single family or duplex uses, except that replacement trees will be considered protected trees even if planted on lots smaller than two acres that have single family or duplex uses. This means that if a replacement tree is planted on a lot smaller than two acres with a single family use, and the owner of that lot were to one day remove the tree, he would have to replace that tree in accordance with this section.

(b) Replacing trees.

(1) Tree mitigation may be accomplished by planting replacement trees anywhere in this district.

(2) Except in the tree conservation area, the building official shall give tree mitigation credit of two caliper inches for every caliper inch of a protected tree with a caliper of 18 inches or more that is preserved within this district.

(c) Mitigation required. A minimum of 15,569 caliper inches must be mitigated.

(d) Tree conservation area.

(1) In general. Tree mitigation may also be accomplished by establishing a tree conservation area consistent with the conceptual plan. A tree conservation area is established if the building official approves the tree conservation area plan.

(2) Tree conservation area plan. A tree conservation area plan must be submitted to the building official. The tree conservation area plan must include:

(A) A survey of the boundaries of the tree conservation area.

(B) A tree protection plan for the tree conservation area that complies with Section 51A-10.136.

(C) A plan for the preservation and maintenance of the tree conservation area.

(3) Approval. The building official shall approve the tree conservation area if the building official determines that the tree conservation area is consistent with the conceptual plan and that the requirements for a tree conservation area plan have been met.

(4) Preliminary and final plats. The tree conservation area must be shown on the preliminary and final plats for areas covering or adjacent to the tree conservation area.

(5) General prohibition on tree removal from the tree conservation area. Tree removal from the tree conservation area is generally prohibited. Pedestrian pathways may be located within the tree conservation area, subject to the following conditions:

(A) Trees under two caliper inches may be removed to create pedestrian pathways.

(B) Pedestrian pathways must be natural, hand-cut footpaths of dirt, gravel, mulch, crushed rock, or natural stones. Asphalt, concrete, or other impervious pathways are prohibited.

(C) Lighting and public furniture along pedestrian pathways is permitted.

(D) Dead or diseased trees, storm-damaged trees, or fallen tree limbs located on or within 20 feet of a pedestrian pathway may be removed at any time.

(E) Pruning of trees within 20 feet of a pedestrian pathway is permitted.

(F) Dead or diseased trees located more than 20 feet from a pedestrian pathway may be removed subject to approval by the city arborist. The city arborist shall prohibit the removal of dead or diseased trees if their removal will create an unreasonably hazardous condition or cause a significant disruption to the natural ecological balance within the tree conservation area.

(6) Mitigation credit.

(A) If the total of all tree conservation areas are a minimum of 30 acres, the responsible party will receive 65 percent credit for the total caliper of required replacement trees.

(B) If additional contiguous woodland tree conservation areas of at least five acres are provided and approved as part of the tree conservation area plan, an additional mitigation credit of five percent may be provided for each additional area, up to a maximum credit of 80 percent of the total caliper of required replacement trees.

(e) Completion date. Tree mitigation must be completed by December 31, 2019. The commission may extend the deadline for completion if significant delays result from the permitting process or the installation of public improvements. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Open Space And Pedestrian Links
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.116. OPEN SPACE AND PEDESTRIAN LINKS.

(a) A community wide trail and sidewalk system must be established to connect the open spaces and tree conservation areas shown on the conceptual plan. Streets must be open to open spaces and tree conservation areas where practical. Natural trail materials, such as mulch or crushed granite, must be used where practical in tree conservation areas. Where streets are adjacent to open space and tree conservation areas and where paths or trails have been provided in the open space or tree conservation areas, sidewalks will not be required in the street right-of- way.

(b) A pedestrian link must be provided to connect Subdistrict 1 with a potential school site in Subdistrict 2, subject to approval by the owners of all utility easements the pedestrian link will cross. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Paving And Infrastructure Design
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.117. PAVING AND INFRASTRUCTURE DESIGN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, paving and infrastructure design must be in accordance with Article VIII.

(b) Collector street.

(1) The collector street, shown and labeled on the conceptual plan, must consist of 37 feet of pavement, measured from the back of the curb, within a 60-foot right-of- way. The collector street may divide in places as shown on the conceptual plan. Each section must consist of 19 feet of pavement, measured from the back of the curb, within a 40-foot right- of-way.

(2) The collector street must generally be single loaded with lots, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(c) Street curbs may be mountable type.

(d) Lots adjacent to a tree conservation area may be platted with access only to an alley, provided a sidewalk is provided in a public easement connecting to street right-of-way. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.118. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) The city council may establish one or more public improvement districts in this district in accordance with Chapter 372 of the Texas Local Government Code to facilitate the acquisition, construction, or improvement of public infrastructure, to provide additional city services, or for any other lawful purpose, to the full extent such action is authorized under the law.

(d) A development plan or preliminary plat may not be submitted for any development which includes lots less than one acre in area until:

(1) a traffic impact analysis has been approved by the director; and

(2) a development agreement has been approved by the city council that details infrastructure and service provisions and phasing, and assigns cost responsibilities for the provision of emergency services, water, wastewater, and solid waste disposal.

(e) Monument features, entrance signage, landscaping, and irrigation is allowed within the city right-of-way.

(f) Access from a public right-of-way must be provided to the cemetery shown on the conceptual plan during the official visiting hours established under Section 11-19. The cemetery must be reflected on any preliminary or final plats of the area. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.119. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 27921)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-818.120. ZONING MAP.

PD 818 is located on Zoning Map Nos. G-13 and H-13. (Ord. 27921)
